rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the people worse in place transfers evil from its inhabitants to their location; the metonymy intensifies the judgment beyond simply calling them worse and more astray.
rows.anchor: ﴿ شر مكانا ﴾ جعلت الشرارة للمكان وهي لأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns hypocritical Jews who professed faith before the Prophet; God disclosed that they left his assembly as unbelieving and untouched by his reminders.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ناس من اليهود كانوا يدخلون على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يظهرون له الإيمان نفاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases “in disbelief” and “with it” are circumstantial expressions: they entered as unbelievers and left as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقوله ( بالكفر ) و ( به ) حالان أي دخلوا كافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle qad brings the past close to the present and conveys expectation: hypocrisy was evident, and the Prophet expected God to expose what they concealed; it describes their state when they said they believed.
rows.anchor: ولمعنى آخر وهو ان أمارات النفاق كانت لائحة عليهم وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوقعا لإظهار الله ما كتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥurum means people in consecration; intentional killing means killing while remembering consecration or knowing the animal is protected, whereas the described mistaken cases are errors.
rows.anchor: محرمون جمع حرام كردح في جمع رداح والتعمد ان يقتله وهو ذاكر لاحرامه أو عالم ان ما يقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ihram prohibitions also cover mistakes, the verse conditions liability on intention because its occasion involved deliberate hunting; error is included by extension as a stricter rule.
rows.anchor: لأن مورد الآية فيمن تعمد فقد روي أنه عن لهم في عمرة الحديبية حمار وحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a wild ass appeared during the Hudaybiyya lesser pilgrimage; Abu al-Yusr killed it with his spear, was told he had hunted while consecrated, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أنه عن لهم في عمرة الحديبية حمار وحش فحمل عليه أبو اليسر فطعنه برمحه

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī distinguishes the rule: scripture addresses deliberate killing, while the Sunna addresses mistaken killing.
rows.anchor: وعن الزهري نزل الكتاب بالعمد ووردت السنة بالخطأ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr sees no expiation for mistaken killing, relying on the verse's condition of intention.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير لا أرى في الخطا شيئا أخذا باشتراط العمد في الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Two transmitted opinions are attributed to al-Ḥasan on this issue, though their contents are not specified here.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن روايتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading of jazāʾ and mithl means that the offender owes compensation equivalent to the game killed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فجزاء مثل ما قتل ﴾ برفع جزاء ومثل جميعا بمعنى فعليه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa defines the equivalent as the killed animal's monetary value, assessed where it was hunted.
rows.anchor: وهو عند أبي حنيفة قيمة المصيد يقوم حيث صيد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If the valuation reaches the cost of an offering, the offender may buy livestock of that value, feed the poor from its value, or fast one day for each person's food; a remainder below one person's portion can be fasted for a day or given in charity.
rows.anchor: فإن بلغت قيمته ثمن هدى تخير بين ان يهدي من النعم ما قيمته قيمة الصيد

rows.speaker: محمد والشافعي
rows.claim: Muḥammad and al-Shāfiʿī require a corresponding livestock animal; if no equivalent animal exists, they turn to Abū Ḥanīfa's valuation method.
rows.anchor: وعند محمد والشافعي رحمهما الله مثله نظيره من النعم فإن لم يوجد له نظير من النعم عدل إلى قول أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The value-based view can explain “from livestock” and “an offering reaching the Kaaba”: the offender may buy and sacrifice livestock with the assessed value.
rows.anchor: قد خير من أوجب القيمة بين ان يشتري بها هديا أو طعاما أو يصوم كما خير الله تعالى في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Valuation best explains the verse's three-way choice: first assess the game, then choose sacrifice, feeding, or fasting; requiring an animal analogue alone makes the later choices fit only cases without an analogue.
rows.anchor: على ان التخيير الذي هو في الآية بين ان يجزي بالهدى أو يكفر بالاطعام أو بالصوم إنما يستقيم استقامة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads fa-jazāʾuhu mithlu mā qatala, explicitly supplying the possessive pronoun in the compensation phrase.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله فجزاؤه مثل ما قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A genitive reading annexes jazāʾ to mithl; its underlying construction has mithl in the accusative, as in the example “I wondered at Zayd's striking.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء فجزاء مثل ما قتل على الاضافة وأصله فجزاء مثل ما قتل بنصب مثل

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads the original accusative construction with mithl as the object of the compensation phrase.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي على الأصل

rows.speaker: محمد بن مقاتل
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil reads both jazāʾ and mithl in the accusative, meaning the offender should pay compensation equivalent to what he killed.
rows.anchor: وقرا محمد بن مقاتل فجزاء مثل ما قتل بنصبهما بمعنى فليجز جزاء مثل ما قتل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads naʿam with a silent ʿayn, avoiding a difficult vowel on a guttural consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرا الحسن من النعم بسكون العين استثقل الحركة على حرف الحلق فسكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in yaḥkumu bihi refers to a judgment by the same kind of animal as the one killed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يحكم به ﴾ بمثل ما قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two just persons are two equitable Muslim arbiters; the need for valuation and deliberation is offered as evidence for the value interpretation.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذوا عدل منكم ﴾ حكمان عادلان من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabīṣa, after hunting a gazelle while consecrated, asked ʿUmar, who consulted ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ordered a sheep; when Qabīṣa disparaged the consultation, ʿUmar struck him and invoked the verse about two just arbiters.
rows.anchor: وعن قبيصة انه أصاب ظبيا وهو محرم فسال عمر فشاور عبد الرحمن بن عوف ثم امره بذبح شاة

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar reads dhū ʿadlin in the singular, meaning any just person who judges, rather than one arbiter alone.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن جعفر ( ذو عدل منكم ) أراد يحكم به من يعدل منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the imam is intended by the phrase about the two just arbiters.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد الامام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadyan can be parsed as a circumstantial modifier of jazāʾ, an apposition to mithl or its case, or a circumstantial modifier of the pronoun in bihi.
rows.anchor: حال عن جزاء فيمن وصفه بمثل لأن الصفة خصصته فقربته من المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baligh al-kaʿba describes the offering because its annexation is not literal; reaching the Kaaba means slaughtering within the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بالغ الكعبة ﴾ لأن اضافته غير حقيقية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits distributing the offering wherever one wishes, while al-Shāfiʿī requires distribution in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فاما التصدق به فحيث شئت عند أبي حنيفة وعند الشافعي في الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When jazāʾ is accusative, kaffāra may be the predicate of an omitted subject, or part of an estimated obligation coordinated with compensation.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كفارة ﴾ من ينصب جزاء قلت يجعلها خبر مبتدا محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading kaffāratu ṭaʿāmi masākīn means an expiation consisting of food, like a ring made of silver.
rows.anchor: وقرىء أو كفارة طعام مساكين على الاضافة وهذه الإضافة مبينة

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads miskīn in the singular because it functions as an explanatory term and denotes the category.
rows.anchor: وقرا الأعرج أو كفارة طعام مسكين وانما وحد لأنه واقع موقع التبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, ʿadl is an equivalent of another kind, such as fasting or feeding; with fatḥa, ʿadl is equivalence in amount. The fatḥa denotes the verbal noun, the kasra the thing balanced against another.
rows.anchor: وقرىء أو عدل ذلك بكسر العين والفرق بينهما أن عدل الشيء ما عادله من غير جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika points to the food, and ṣiyāman is an explanatory accusative for ʿadl, as in saying “I have his equal in men.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ اشارة إلى الطعام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf let the hunter choose the form of expiation; Muḥammad assigns the choice about fasting to the two arbiters.
rows.anchor: والخيار في ذلك إلى قاتل الصيد عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وعند محمد إلى الحكمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause attaches to the compensation command: the offender must compensate or atone so he tastes the bad consequence of violating ihram's sanctity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ليذوق ﴾ متعلق بقوله ( فجزاء ) أي فعليه ان يجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabāl means an unpleasant, harmful consequence that weighs on a person; the Qur'anic phrase in 73:16 uses it in the sense of something heavy.
rows.anchor: والوبال المكروه والضرر الذي يناله في العاقبة من عمل سوء لثقله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wabīl food is heavy on the stomach and is not easily digested.
rows.anchor: والطعام الوبيل الذي يثقل على المعدة فلا يستمرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pardoned hunting during ihram before the believers consulted the Messenger about whether it was permitted.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عفا الله عما سلف ﴾ لكم من الصيد في حال الاحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the pardon to concern pre-Islamic hunting, since the people followed earlier revealed laws in which hunting was forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقيل عما سلف لكم في الجاهلية منه لأنهم كانوا متعبدين بشرائع من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning means killing game while consecrated again after the prohibition was revealed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن عاد ﴾ إلى قتل الصيد وهو محرم بعد نزول النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fayantakimu is the predicate of an omitted subject, hence the introductory fa; the threat means God will exact retribution in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ينتقم خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره فهو ينتقم منه ولذلك دخلت الفاء

rows.speaker: عطاء وإبراهيم وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وعامة العلماء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, Ibrāhīm, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, and the majority require expiation from someone who repeats the offense.
rows.anchor: اختلف في وجوب الكفارة على العائد فعن عطاء وابراهيم وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وجوبها وعليه عامة العلماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Shurayḥ say a repeat offender owes no expiation, relying on the verse's apparent wording, which does not mention one.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وشريح أنه لا كفارة عليه تعلقا بالظاهر وانه لم يذكر الكفارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-inẓur makes looking the purpose of travel: travel to observe, not heedlessly. Thumma unẓur permits travel for trade and other benefits while making reflection on destroyed peoples obligatory, separating the required act from the permitted journey.
rows.anchor: جعل النظر مسببا السير في قوله : { فانظروا } فكأنه قيل سيروا لأجل النظر

none: The segment is broken and contains only an opening brace.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāytakum means “tell me”; its second-person suffix has no syntactic position, since assigning one would make the sentence falsely mean “did you see yourself?”
rows.anchor: أرأيتكم } أخبروني . والضمير الثاني لا محل له من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted question is whom the polytheists would call if God's punishment or the Hour came; the rebuke asks whether they call their idols in distress or single out God.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق الاستخبار محذوف ، تقديره : إن أتاكم عذاب الله { أو أتتكم الساعة } من تدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call on God alone, who can remove distress if He wills without harm; they forget their idols because their minds are absorbed in remembering the only one able to relieve it.
rows.anchor: بل تخصونه بالدعاء دون الآلهة { فيكشف ما تدعون إليه } أي ما تدعون إلى كشفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may instead be attached to “do you call on other than God?”; even when the Hour is included, removal is conditioned on God's will, signaling that a wiser consideration prevents it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق الاستخبار بقوله : { أغير الله تدعون } كأنه قيل : أغير الله تدعون إن أتاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baʾsāʾ means hardship and al-ḍarrāʾ harm; another gloss gives famine and hunger for the first, and illness plus loss of wealth and lives for the second.
rows.anchor: البأساء ، والضراء : البؤس ، والضر . وقيل : البأساء : القحط والجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent messengers to earlier peoples, who rejected them, then afflicted those peoples so they might humble themselves, become contrite, and repent.
rows.anchor: ولقد أرسلنا إليهم الرسل فكذبوهم فأخذناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā here denies that they humbled themselves; their only excuse was stubbornness, hard hearts, and pride in deeds Satan had made attractive.
rows.anchor: معناه : نفي التضرع ، كأنه قيل : فلم يتضرعوا إذ جاءهم بأسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting what they were reminded of means neglecting the lesson of hardship, which neither benefited nor deterred them.
rows.anchor: أي تركوا الاتعاظ به ولم ينفع فيهم ولم يزجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening every door means granting health, abundance, and varied blessings, alternating hardship and ease like a caring father who alternates severity and kindness to reform his child.
rows.anchor: من الصحة والسعة وصنوف النعمة ، ليزاوج عليهم بين نوبتي الضراء والسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they rejoiced over what they received, their joy became arrogance without gratitude, repentance, or apology.
rows.anchor: أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون } واجمون ، متحسرون آيسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mublisūn means stunned, sorrowful, and despairing.
rows.anchor: مبلسون } واجمون ، متحسرون آيسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting off the people's dābir means leaving no one alive and utterly exterminating them.
rows.anchor: فقطع دابر القوم } آخرهم لم يترك منهم أحد ، قد استؤصلت شأفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing praise signals that praising God at the destruction of wrongdoers is obligatory and that this destruction is among the greatest blessings.
rows.anchor: والحمد لله رب العالمين } إيذان بوجوب الحمد عند هلاك الظلمة ، وأنه من أجل النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation reads fattaḥnā with a doubled tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { فتحنا } بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about taking religion as play can mean that idolatry and pagan prohibitions were unserious practices driven by desire and appetite.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عبدة الأصنام وما كانوا عليه من تحريم البحائر والسوائب وغير ذلك ، من باب اللعب واللهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the idolaters made worship of idols and similar amusements into their religion.
rows.anchor: و اتخذوا ما هو لعب ولهو من عبادة الأصنام وغيرها دينا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that they mocked Islam, the religion they were commanded to follow and invited to accept.
rows.anchor: واتخذوا دينهم الذي كلفوه ودعوا إليه وهو دين الإسلام لعبا ولهوا ، حيث سخروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God gave every people a festival for prayer and remembrance; polytheists and scriptural communities turned theirs into amusement, unlike Muslims who observe theirs as prescribed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جعل الله لكل قوم عيدا يعظمونه ويصلون فيه ويعمرونه بذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Leave them” means turn away, disregard their denial and mockery, and do not let them occupy the heart; “remind by it” means remind them with the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( ذرهم ) أعرض عنهم ، ولا تبال بتكذيبهم واستهزائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An tubsala nafs means lest a soul be handed over to ruin and punishment and held hostage by its evil deeds; ibsāl originally means preventing the person handed over.
rows.anchor: { أن تبسل نفس } مخافة أن تسلم إلى الهلكة والعذاب وترتهن بسوء كسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem illustrates ibsāl as handing over one's sons without cause; basl also means something forbidden, and bāsil describes a fierce or severely frowning person.
rows.anchor: وإبسالي بني بغير جرم … بعوناه ولا بدم مراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdl means ransom because the redeemer gives an equivalent for the one ransomed; kullu ʿadlin is accusative as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وإن تفد كل فداء ، والعدل الفدية . لأن الفادي يعدل المفدي بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse the subject of passive yukhadh is minhā, not ʿadl, because ʿadl is a verbal noun; in 2:48 it means the ransom object, so it can be the subject.
rows.anchor: وفاعل { يؤخذ } قوله : { منها } لا ضمير العدل لأن العدل ههنا مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulāʾika points to the people who made their religion play and amusement.
rows.anchor: { أولائك } إشارة إلى المتخذين دينهم لعبا ولهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An occasion report says the verse was revealed about ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Bakr's son, when he invited his father to worship idols.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه حين دعاه ابنه عبد الرحمن إلى عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anadʿū means “shall we worship”; the beings besides God are idols unable to benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: أنعبد { من دون الله } الضار النافع ما لا يقدر على نفعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning on one's heels means reverting to shirk after God rescued and guided the believers to Islam.
rows.anchor: ونرد على أعقابنا } راجعين إلى الشرك بعد إذ أنقذنا الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison depicts someone whom rebellious jinn or ghouls have carried into a desolate place, confused and lost, while companions call him toward the straight road and he ignores them; this reflects Arab beliefs about jinn.
rows.anchor: كالذي ذهبت به مردة الجن والغيلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is a circumstantial expression attached to the pronoun in nardu: would the believers turn back resembling the one carried away by devils?
rows.anchor: قلت النصب على الحال من الضمير في { نرد * على أعقابنا } أي : أننكص مشبهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison also resembles the Qur'anic image of someone whom Satan buffets into madness.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { كالذى * يتخبطه الشيطان من المس } ( البقرة : 275 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance is Islam alone; all beyond it is error, as affirmed by the verses on seeking a religion other than Islam and on what lies beyond truth.
rows.anchor: وهو الإسلام { هو الهدى } وحده وما وراءه ضلال وغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amran is accusative, coordinated with the syntactic position of “God's guidance is the guidance,” so both are statements to be conveyed.
rows.anchor: قلت : النصب عطفا على محل قوله : { إن هدى الله هو الهدى } على أنهما مقولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in linuslima gives the purpose: believers were commanded or told to submit so that they would submit.
rows.anchor: قلت : هي تعليل للأمر ، بمعنى : أمرنا وقيل لنا أسلموا لأجل أن نسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the passage may concern Abū Bakr, the Prophet is told to say this because of the unity between him and the believers, especially his bond with Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: قلت : للاتحاد الذي كان بين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين ، خصوصا بينه وبين الصديق أبي بكر

none: The segment contains verse text only, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following most people on earth would lead believers astray because most people usually follow their whims.
rows.anchor: أي من الناس أضلوك ، لأن الأكثر في غالب الأمر يتبعون هواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conjecture is that their ancestors were right, so they imitate them; alternatively, they fabricate claims about what God prohibited and permitted.
rows.anchor: وهو ظنهم أن آباءهم كانوا على الحق فهم يقلدونهم { وإن هم إلا يخرصون } يقدرون أنهم على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manifest and hidden sin can mean what people disclose and conceal, or what they do and intend.
rows.anchor: { ظاهر الإثم وباطنه } ما أعلنتم منه وما أسررتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes manifest sin as fornication in brothels and hidden sin as secret relations with a lover.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ظاهره الزنا في الحوانيت ، وباطنه الصديقة في السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAshr amthālihā puts an adjective denoting the kind in place of its noun: ten good deeds like it are meant.
rows.anchor: {عشر أمثالها } على إقامة صفة الجنس المميز مقام الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation raises both words in ʿashru amthālihā, treating them as adjectives.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( عشر أمثالها ) برفعهما جميعا على الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tenfold reward is the minimum promised multiplication; elsewhere reward is promised seven hundredfold or without reckoning.
rows.anchor: وهذا أقل ما وعد من الإضعاف . وقد وعد بالواحد سبعمائة ، ووعد ثوابا بغير حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multiplying good deeds is divine generosity, while requiting evil deeds is justice; people are not deprived of reward or given extra punishment.
rows.anchor: ومضاعفة الحسنات فضل ، ومكافأة السيئات عدل { وهم لا يظلمون } لا ينقص من ثوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs was granted respite to test people; resisting temptation earns great reward, as do the worldly adornments, pleasures, and desires created for testing servants.
rows.anchor: لما في ذلك من ابتلاء العباد ، وفي مخالفته من أعظم الثواب ، وحكمه حكم ما خلق في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fabi-mā aghwaytanī means “because You caused me to go astray”; the command to bow led to his error, unlike the steadfast angels, though they and Adam are nobler in nature and rank.
rows.anchor: فبسبب إغوائك إياي لأقعدن لهم . وهو تكليفه إياه ما وقع به في الغي

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says Iblīs meant that God commanded him to prostrate, and pride then drove him to disobey.
rows.anchor: وعن الأصم : أمرتني بالسجود فحملني الأنف على معصيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that, having fallen into error, Iblīs would work hard to mislead people and corrupt them as he had been corrupted through them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : فبسبب وقوعي في الغي لأجتهدن في إغوائهم حتى يفسدوا بسببي ، كما فسدت بسببهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the oath lām prevents the causal bāʾ from attaching to la-aqʿudanna, the bāʾ attaches to an omitted oath verb: “because You misled me, I swear by God.”
rows.anchor: تعلقت بفعل القسم المحذوف تقديره : فبما أغويتني أقسم بالله لأقعدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the bāʾ is itself an oath; Iblīs swore by the misguidance because divine legal charge exposes servants to everlasting happiness and is therefore among God's best acts.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الباء للقسم ، أي : فأقسم بإغوائك لأقعدن ، وإنما أقسم بالإغواء ؛ لأنه كان تكليفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author attacks the compulsionists' fabricated story about Ṭāwūs and a jurist: it portrays Iblīs as more knowledgeable than someone who says he misleads himself, and accuses these theologians of attributing evil to God and inventing reports.
rows.anchor: ومن تكاذيب المجبرة ما حكوه عن طاوس : أنه كان في المسجد الحرام فجاء رجل من كبار الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes mā as an interrogative, “by what did You mislead me?”, then begins la-aqʿudanna as a new clause; retaining alif after a preposition with interrogative mā is rare and irregular.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { ما } للاستفهام ، كأنه قيل : بأي شيء أغويتني ، ثم ابتدىء لأقعدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ghayy means corruption; the example ghawiya al-faṣīl describes a calf whose stomach is spoiled by overfeeding.
rows.anchor: وأصل الغي الفساد . ومنه : غوى الفصيل ، إذا بشم . والبشم : فساد في المعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La-aqʿudanna lahum ṣirāṭaka means Iblīs will obstruct the Islamic path as an enemy blocks travelers; its accusative is adverbial, like the cited Arabic usages and poem.
rows.anchor: لأعترضن لهم على طريق الإسلام كما يعترض العدو على الطريق ليقطعه على السابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source cites the poetic line “kamā ʿasala al-ṭarīqa al-thaʿlab” as evidence for the adverbial construction of sitting across a road.
rows.anchor: كما عسل الطريق الثعلب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan waits along Adam's ways: he urges a return to ancestral religion, abandonment of one's home for migration, and avoidance of fighting; the believer resists each appeal and proceeds to faith, migration, and jihad.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان قعد لابن آدم بأطرقه : قعد له بطريق الإسلام فقال له : تدع دين آبائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming at people from four directions represents Satan's attempts to whisper and tempt as far as he can, linked to the command in 17:64.
rows.anchor: من الجهات الأربع التي يأتي منها العدو في الغالب . وهذا مثل لوسوسته إليهم وتسويله ما أمكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different prepositions before front/back and right/left are adverbial complements; Arabic varies these governing particles by usage, which is learned from speech rather than generalized by analogy.
rows.anchor: المفعول فيه عدي إليه الفعل نحو تعديته إلى المفعول به . فكما اختلفت حروف التعدية في ذاك اختلفت في هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlā yamīnihi means positioned at or over the right, while ʿan yamīnihi originally means separated and turned away from the companion, though it later came to cover both senses.
rows.anchor: أنه تمكن من جهة اليمين تمكن المستعلي من المستعلى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variants rami-tu ʿan, ʿalā, or min al-qaws reflect an arrow's distance from, position on, or beginning point at the bow; between and behind can mean within those directions, while min bayni indicates a portion of them.
rows.anchor: ونحوه من المفعول به قولهم رميت عن القوس ، وعلى القوس ، ومن القوس ؛ لأن السهم يبعد عنها

rows.speaker: شقيق
rows.claim: Shuqayq says Satan waits at four posts each morning: he tempts with complacency about forgiveness, fear of failing dependents, desire for praise, and appetite; he counters each with verses about repentance, God's provision, the pious end, and separation from desires.
rows.anchor: وعن شقيق : ما من صباح إلا قعد لي الشيطان على أربع مراصد : من بين يدي ، ومن خلفي ، وعن يميني ، وعن شمالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs' expectation that most people would not be grateful is presented as conjecture, confirmed by 34:20; another view says he learned it from angels whom God informed.
rows.anchor: قاله تظنينا ، بدليل قوله : { ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه }
